hammel

Hammel is a standalone demographic microsimulator with an R interface and a C++17 engine. It models continuous-time mortality, fertility, and union formation, dissolution, remarriage, and optional cohabitation/conversion, with group-specific rates, individual group transitions, partner matching, ancestry, and newborn identity inheritance. Results expose person, union, and transition histories as tibbles.

Milestones 1–6 are complete by user acceptance: mortality/fertility, union formation, groups, dissolution/remarriage/cohabitation, parity-specific fertility with persistent fertility heterogeneity, and individual group transitions (D116). Milestone 7, time-varying inputs, is next. See the documentation index, scientific contract, and validation record for implemented behavior and limitations. Future mechanisms are listed in the roadmap.

Installation

You can install the development version of hammel from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("AaronGullickson/hammel")

Example

The union-formation example demonstrates model construction and simulation. The user-authored milestone 3 report assesses group-specific rates, matching, ancestry, inheritance, and performance. Rendering the report installs the package, retrieves HMD rates, and runs substantial simulations; ordinary package tests use offline inputs unless live database tests are explicitly enabled.

The milestone 4 report and its rendered assessment cover dissolution, age/duration remarriage, cohabitation, conversion, separate matching roles, and performance. The user accepted milestone 4 on October 29, 2026 (D093). Rendering retrieves HMD mortality, runs 100 independently initialized replications per scenario, and executes the offline test suite. See validation contents for retained reports, inputs, and supporting diagnostic evidence.

The accepted milestone 5 report and rendered assessment cover parity-specific fertility, cell-accounted birth spacing, restart and union-type rate checks, and lognormal fertility weights with maternal inheritance (D105). Completion retains the documented sparse-cell/unrealized-intensity and reproductive-selection limitations. Rendering installs the package, retrieves HFD/HMD inputs, runs replications and the offline tests; it is not an ordinary package check.

The accepted milestone 6 report and rendered assessment cover age/duration transitions, sex/union-type strata, demographic rate and formation-group recovery, population shares and performance (D116, October 30, 2026). The final render was active at acceptance; preserve its intermediates until it finishes. Household moves are deferred to the regions milestone (D114).
